gap: B spends 63px of the 908px viewport on a top bar that never recedes (hairline #dfdfdf at y=63, body text guillotined mid-x-height beneath it), and fills that space with a fake title — the truncated first line "went Alice like the wind, and was just…" in #8c8c8c, dead-centre in the eye's path, re-rendering every time the opening sentence is rewritten. A spends nothing up there: 861px of writing surface vs B's 792px, +8.7%, with no title noise at all.
gapTheirs: A's status bar is set in the same ink as the prose — sampled #191919 in the bar vs #191919 in the body, zero tonal separation — and it runs six metrics at once across a ~925px band ("62.476 Characters / 50.637 Without Spaces / 12.072 Words / 772 Sentences / 01:00:21 Reading Time", plus Tasks checked), all one size, one weight, no number/label hierarchy. B's bar carries three (113 words / 556 characters / < 1 min read) with numerals at #4a4a4a and labels ~#9a9a9a on #f9f9f9, and its menu ends with "Hide Statistics" — A's menu offers only which counters, never off. Net: A's loudest object after the sentence is a row of black numerals; B's is grey.
verdict: B is the one you'd write in, but only just, and for an unglamorous reason: it knows the count is not the sentence. A hands you a bigger canvas — 69 more pixels and a blessedly empty top edge — then parks five near-black metrics along the bottom in the exact ink of your prose, with a menu whose submenu drops over the very bar it's editing and no way to switch the thing off. B's sin is the opposite and cheaper: a 63px lid that never lifts, wearing your first line as a fake, ellipsised title, so you write with your own opening sentence quoted back at you in grey. Fix B by letting the header fade on keystroke and killing the pseudo-title; fixing A means re-toning the whole bar and admitting a writer needs one number, not six.
